title: Familiar Tales - A delightful fantasy adventure
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dlABqtYhbMk

Daniel (@dungeondive) is an online friend of designer Jerry Hawthorne and says so up front, having previously been hard on Aftermath's rulebook and onboarding. Familiar Tales, he reports, has none of those problems — the best Plaid Hat rulebook since Dungeon Run, and a browser-based app that needs no download, runs the enemy turns, tracks danger and campaign choices, and is fully voice acted.

You play four familiars raising a displaced princess across three eras, from infant to young woman, and the choices you make shape who eventually sits on the throne. The baby must be carried and her mood managed; a crying child can alert guards. Failure moves the story forward with misfortune points rather than sending you back to replay.

Skill checks use multi-use cards — might, agility, blocking, insight, plus a movement value, special actions and combo icons — with fatigue cards clogging your deck and adding danger when played. The solo variant merges all four character decks into one, which Daniel prefers to juggling four hands.

He places it as the culmination of the line running from Mice and Mystics through Stuffed Fables and Comanauts to Aftermath, calls the campaign short enough that he'll actually finish it, and admits he had to physically stop playing in order to record the video.

----

Do you finish campaign games, or does the shelf fill with half-played boxes? What campaign length actually gets to your table twice?
